newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Germany repeats aims for 2.9 pct '97 deficit to GDP.
newsitem.headline: Germany repeats aims for 2.9 pct '97 deficit to GDP.

text.p: Germany intends to cut back its public deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product in 1997, a paper to be presented to a meeting of European Finance Ministers in Brussels on Monday showed.

The paper obtained by Reuters, dated February 26, also showed that Germany expected to notch up total outstanding debt of 61.5 percent of GDP in 1997, above the 60 percent reference level laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.

Germany, which had originally aimed to cut its deficits back to 2.5 percent of GDP this year, raised its forecast to 2.9 percent some weeks ago. It has said that the new figure contains all risks posed by a sharp jump in German joblessness at the start of this year.

In the paper, Germany gave the following forecasts for the two key figures, adding that these did not yet incorporate the impact of a planned tax reform, now expected to take effect from 1998, or of proposed pension reform.
(* These figures are not precise forecasts)

Earlier, German Finance Minister Theo Waigel argued that special circumstances such as German unification, high transfers to eastern Europa and Germany's large contributions to the European Union had buoyed German debt.
